question: Assume today is 2026-09-12. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of passengers at London Heathrow Airport in September 2026, as reported in Heathrow's monthly traffic statistics.

target.what: Total passengers passing through London Heathrow Airport (all terminals, arrivals plus departures, domestic and international, as counted in Heathrow's monthly traffic statistics 'passengers' figure) during the calendar month of September 2026
target.publisher: Heathrow Airport Limited (monthly traffic statistics / operational figures)
target.caveats: Target period is future/ongoing relative to the 2026-09-12 cutoff, so no September 2026 actual exists; must be forecast from prior months, seasonality, and capacity signals. Definitional notes: Heathrow's headline 'passengers' counts terminal passengers (arrivals + departures, each traveller counted

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 passengers will follow Heathrow's own seasonal pattern: September is typically below July/August peak and above winter months, with year-over-year growth applied to September 2025 actual. Target = Sept 2025 actual × (1 + recent YoY growth rate).
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow monthly passenger totals for September 2023, September 2024, September 2025, and the most recent months published before 2026-09-12 (e.g., Jan–Jul 2026), plus YoY growth rates. Minimum: Sept 2025 actual and 2026 YTD growth.
search_hints: Heathrow monthly traffic statistics September 2025 passengers

candidates.perspective: CAA / UK Civil Aviation Authority airport statistics
candidates.hypothesis: CAA publishes Heathrow terminal passenger totals that closely track Heathrow's own figures; CAA monthly data for 2025 and early 2026 can supply the September 2025 base and recent trend if Heathrow's own release is incomplete.
candidates.data_to_find: CAA airport data for Heathrow: monthly terminal passengers Sept 2025 and 2026 months available before cutoff; annual 2025 total. Minimum: Sept 2025 monthly figure.
search_hints: CAA Heathrow airport terminal passengers monthly 2025
UK airport data Heathrow passengers September 2025

candidates.hypothesis: Passengers ≈ seats offered × load factor. September 2026 seat capacity at Heathrow from published airline schedules, times an assumed load factor (~82–86%), gives an independent estimate. Direction: higher scheduled seats → higher passengers.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow scheduled seat capacity (departing seats or total two-way seats) for September 2026 from OAG/Cirium summaries or airline schedule press; Heathrow load factor recent values. Minimum: September 2026 departing seat capacity and a load factor.

candidates.hypothesis: Heathrow's passenger numbers are bounded by its daily passenger cap and air transport movements (ATMs). September 2026 passengers ≈ daily cap × 30 × utilisation, or ATMs × average passengers per ATM. Direction: cap/ATM levels constrain the ceiling.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow daily passenger cap for 2026, monthly ATM totals for Sept 2025 and 2026, average passengers per ATM. Minimum: recent monthly ATM count and passengers-per-ATM ratio.

candidates.perspective: Heathrow plc investor guidance and traffic forecasts
candidates.hypothesis: Heathrow's own traffic forecasts and investor reports give expected 2026 passenger growth; applying forecast annual growth to the September 2025 base yields a September 2026 estimate. Direction: guidance growth rate scales the base.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow plc traffic forecasts for 2026, H1 2026 traffic results, any guidance on full-year 2026 passengers. Minimum: a 2026 growth expectation or H1 2026 actuals.

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 passengers may deviate from trend due to strikes, ATC disruptions, weather, or calendar (day-of-week) composition. Quantify exposure: number of strike days, ATC events, and weekday count in September 2026 vs 2025.
candidates.data_to_find: Any announced strikes/disruptions at Heathrow affecting September 2026 (as of cutoff), September 2026 weekday composition, and historical impact of similar disruptions on monthly passengers. Minimum: confirmation of no major disruption or an estimated percentage impact.

candidates.hypothesis: September-to-August and September-to-annual ratios are stable; September 2026 ≈ August 2026 actual × (Sept/Aug seasonal ratio). Direction: if August 2026 is known, apply historical Sept/Aug ratio.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow monthly passengers Aug 2025, Sept 2025, Aug 2026 (if published before cutoff), and historical Sept/Aug ratios for 2023–2025. Minimum: Aug 2026 actual and one historical Sept/Aug ratio.
search_hints: Heathrow monthly passengers August September ratio

assumptions.name: September 2026 YoY change factor vs September 2025
assumptions.rationale: Recent months show mixed YoY: H1 2026 +0.2% (p150), Jan-Aug 2026 -0.4% (p229), July 2026 -1.5% (p46), August 2026 roughly flat to -2% (p205/p227). September 2025 was a record (p1). A modest decline to flat is the central case, with a range spanning continued softness to a small recovery.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 demand tracks the recent 2026 trend rather than a sharp shock.
assumptions.falsified_by: A September 2026 release showing strong growth (>3%) or a steep fall (>5%).

assumptions.name: September/August seasonal ratio
assumptions.rationale: September is typically below the August peak; September 2025 (7.348m) vs August 2025 (8.036m, p207) gives ~0.914, while a milder shoulder season gives ~0.95. Central ~0.935.
assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 seasonal shape resembles recent years.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 is unusually strong or weak relative to August.

assumptions.name: September 2026 load factor
assumptions.rationale: H1 2026 seat factor was 78.8% (p188); historical max ~81% (p101); September is a strong month so a load factor near the upper end of recent experience is plausible.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 load factor is in line with recent Heathrow experience.
assumptions.falsified_by: A reported September 2026 load factor outside 78-86%.

assumptions.name: Domestic share of Heathrow departing seats
assumptions.rationale: UK domestic passengers were ~5% of September 2025 total (p8/p1); domestic seats are a small fraction of total departing seats, used to gross up international seats (p78) to total seats.
assumptions.applies_when: Domestic capacity share in September 2026 is similar to 2025.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that domestic capacity share changed materially.

methods.label: m1
methods.rationale: September 2025 actual scaled by the August 2026/August 2025 ratio (7,866,510/8,035,996 ≈ 0.979). Signal is now August 2025 (p365) vs August 2026 (p205), both August totals, so the year alignment is valid. Assumes September 2026 moves like August 2026 relative to the prior year. Shared dependency: relies on Heathrow's own reported levels.

methods.label: m2

p205.role: Heathrow August 2026 total passengers (latest actual month)

methods.rationale: Bridge from the known August 2026 actual to September 2026 via the historical Sept/Aug ratio (~0.914 from p1/p365). Failure mode: 2026 seasonality differs from 2025; August 2026 was itself a record day month.

methods.label: m4

a1.role: September 2026 YoY change factor vs September 2025

methods.rationale: Direct YoY scaling of the September 2025 actual using the 2026 trend (Jan-Aug -0.4%, August -2.1%, FY guidance -1.1%). Failure mode: September-specific shocks or a different seasonal YoY than the year-to-date trend.

combination.weight_gate: off: inverse backtest-error weights need a bank-level gate (>= 30 scored questions with >= 2 backtested routes, hit rate >= 0.7; METHODS_ZH 4.1), which has not been run

m3.note: Monte Carlo width below the default, not used to narrow

interval.rule: several blocks: root mean square of the block widths, times the Birge ratio when it exceeds 1

baseline.rule: seasonal naive: the target's value for the same calendar period last year

kept.name: September 2026 YoY change factor vs September 2025
kept.rationale: Jan-Aug 2026 is -0.4% YoY (p228/p229), August 2026 -2.1% YoY (p205 vs p207), and company base case is -1.1% for FY2026 (p134/p175). September 2025 was a record September, so a small decline is plausible; range spans -5% to +3%.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 traffic continues the mild 2026 decline seen in recent months.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a strong September 2026 rebound or a sharp new shock (e.g. major ATC/strike disruption).

kept.name: September/August seasonal ratio
kept.rationale: September 2025 (7,348k, p1) divided by August 2025 (8,036k, p365) gives ~0.914; September is consistently below the August peak.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 demand held up unusually close to August levels.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
